origin.description: Drop missing rows, warn, and keep their places in later predictions.

arguments.name: object
arguments.text: A model frame. Pass na_warn as na_action to lm().

origin.details: The warning says how many rows were dropped. predict() without new data puts NA back in those rows, matching na.exclude.
origin.value: Predictions the same length as the original data.
origin.example:
df <- data.frame(x = 1:5, y = c(1, NA, 3, NA, 5))
cat(predict(lm(y ~ x, data = df, na.action = na.warn)), "\n")

translation.description: Drop missing rows, warn, and keep their places in later predictions.

arguments.name: object
arguments.text: A model frame. Pass na_warn as na_action to lm().

translation.details: The warning says how many rows were dropped. predict() without new data puts NA back in those rows, matching na.exclude.
translation.value: Predictions the same length as the original data.
translation.example:
data = {"x": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5], "y": [1.0, None, 3.0, None, 5.0]}
print(predict(lm("y ~ x", data, na_action=na_warn)))
